Press Release:


Farm Murders
Since the start of 2017, 26 farmers have been brutally murdered. Recent statistics indicate that as many as one farm attack a day occurs across the country. Farmers say they’re under siege, but that government is turning a blind eye. Carte Blanche asks: why is this not enough reason to galvanise police and government into action?


Script:


Despite being the shortest month in the year, February saw the most farm murders in a single month since 1990. In 46 attacks,16 people were killed. Over the past 27 years there were 4200 attacks, and 1878 people paid with their lives.
What makes these incidents different from normal crime patterns is that instead of waiting until there is no one home, they seem to deliberately wait for the victims to arrive. They are then often tortured in the most barbaric ways before being killed or left for dead.

Black farmers constitute around 6% of SA's commercial farmers, and, correspondingly around 6% of those attacked or murdered are black. The National African Farmers Union says violent crime goes hand in hand with all rural life.
Aggrey
The rural attacks that are happening, is happening on a daily basis – you can't understand what is happening. Whilst we are sitting here in Johannesburg, our mothers are being raped on a daily basis, in our rural areas, our sisters are being attacked on a daily basis. It's not a private farm of mr Serfontein, of mr Jansen. The criminals are attacking everybody where they see that is vulnerable.
Devi
It is hotly debated whether this is simply random crime, or an organised terror campaign.

While white farmers agree that some attacks have other causes, they feel that reckless politicians, trying to score points are adding fuel to the fire.
Black First land First, say they don't support murders, but they don't have much sympathy with the white farmers
Black first land first
We do understand that black people are upset and angry, and rightfully so because land has been stolen historically and it needs to be returned. And so if black people are responding to that violence with violence – then they are well in their rights to take back land by any means neccesary.

Inciting violence is one thing, but hiring assassins is another. We received a copy of a very interesting conversation between a national intelligence agent and a so called general of the notorious prison gang the 28's. He spent more than 20 years in jail for farm murders and was released in December
Recording
Hulle't my ook gese binnekant wanneer ek uitkom moet ek kontak maak met Julius Malema, die ou van limpopo van die EFF. Want hy was ook nou hier, nou in Sept, toe was Julius malema toe was hy blykbaar Pretoria toe, New Lock. Toe kom hy daar, by New Lock, toe vra hy daar, toe se hy daar wanneer julle bendes wil, 'n goue span he, wanneer julle wil 'n span he, kom check my by Limpopo. Ek kan julle 'n span gee. Wat ek julle gaan gee daar is 'n balaclava, 'n gun en cash. Want hy se reguit hy is teen die boere, Julius malema, hy se julle moet net vir my 'n paar moorde pleeg, op boere, plase

They also told me that when I get out, I have to contact Julius Malema, the guy from Limpopo, the EFF. He was also here now in September, Julius Malema apparently went to Pretoria, to New Lock. When he got there, at New Lock, he asked, he said, when you gangs want, a golden team, when you want a team, come and see me in Limpopo. I can give you a team. What I will give you is a balaclava, a gun, and cash. He says straight that he is against farmers, Julius Malema, he says you only have murder a few farmers on farms.

We invited mr malema to respond to us either on camera or in writing, but simply received a one line reply from the EFF stating that:
The CIC is not available to take the interview due to his busy schedule.

This very serious accusation is still unverified, but until mr malema responds, it remains extremely worrying.

Fanus farms in Levubu in the Soutpansberg. His neighbour was murdered recently
Sequence
Hyt hier ingery, opgery oppad na sy huis toe, waar hulle op sy bakkie gespring het min of meer hier, en hom met n mes begin steek het deur die venster wat oop was. Sy skouer. Hy't teruggestoot en toe met spoed weggetrek en die stuurwiel het gesluit en tot stilstand gekom daar waar my voertuig staan. Hulle't hom daar uitgehaal uit sy voertuig uit, hulle't hom teruggesleep, al die pad terug, omtrent 50m van waar die bakkie staan.
He drove in here, up to his house. They jumped on the bakkie and started stabbing him through the open window. His shoulder. He reversed and pulled off with speed and the steering wheel locked and came to a standstill there where my vehicle is standing now. They pulled him out and dragged him all the way back, about 50m from where the bakkie is.

The children were still too traumatised to speak to us. They are trying to get the farm going again.
One of the first farm murders in the region happened in the Bandelierkop district. Ernest Breytenbach now lives in the same house his dad lived in before him
Ernest
They actually put the number plates of the bakkie at his feet. And the stoplights, they tied it to his feet with electrical wire, as well as the front flicker lights, they also tied by the sides of his head. And they actually left him like that.

All the farmers in the area helped to search for his dad
Ernest
My one cousin that was also with me, he actually came from the front and when I saw my father I actually fainted

This happened 19 years ago, but Ernest will never forget that day
Ernest
We aren't totally over it at the moment, but its still in our thoughts and our minds. Anything could happen again, any moment, and we have to prepare ourselves for any type of... anything that could happen

Herman also now lives in the house of his murdered father
Herman
Dit vat jou 10jaar om weer normaal te lewe. Die eerste tien jaar was baie moeilik, hulle se die meest boerderye na so plaasaanval misluk, dit gaan nie aan nie, dit word gestaak. Ek het dit self ervaar. Jy kan nie meer nie, in die aand ry en 'n pomp te gaan afsit nie. Ons is besproeiingsboere, ons het pompe wat ons deur die nag moet aan en af sit
It takes you about 10 years to live normally again. The first 10 years were very difficult. They say after such an attack most farms fail, production stops, it is halted. I also experienced it. You can't drive at night anymore to switch the pumps off. We are irrigation farmers, we have pumps that have to be switched on or off at night.

The remoteness of the homesteads coupled with the relentless attacks, torture and murders changed their lifestyles forever.

The farmers have been forced to take responsibility for their own safety
Fanus
Ek het staalhokke gemaak wat buite die vensters op is, dat hy nie kan inkom nie – 'n staalhok, met nog diefwering by die venster. Dot gaan my daai voorsprong gee. Ek gaan hoor as hy aan daai staalhok breek
I made steel cages and put them up outside the windows, so that he cannot get in. A steel cage, still with burglar proofing on the windows also. It will give me that edge. I will hear when he tries to break the steel cage.

Fanie is another levubu farmer who has had to adapt
Fanie
Hoe verkeerd is dit dat ek 'n kind van 10jaar en agt jaar moet leer om 'n wapen te hanteer. Net vir daai eendag ingeval, net as pappa of mamma seergekry het, en hulle moet hulleself kan verdedig
How wrong is it that I have to teach a child of ten and one of 8 years old to handle a firearm? Just in case, for that one day, when daddy or mommy is injured and they have to defend themselves.

And every day at sunset the idyllic surroundings make way for the same repetitive nightmare
Herman
Die aand het 'n ritueel waardeur jy gaan. Al jou wapens, jou kluis word oopgesluit, jou wapens word reggesit. Wapens word nagegaan, radios word getoets. Dis 'n heeltemaal ander lewe as wat ons gewoond was
The evening has a ritual you have to go through. All your weapons… the gun safe is unlocked, you get the firearms in place. You check your guns, radios are tested. It is a totally different life to the one we were used to.
Fanus

Voor dit donker is, is ons in die huis, dan maak ek seker al die deure is gesluit. Ek maak seker my wapen is reg, is by my, my vrou se wapen is by haar.
Before dark, we are in the house, then I check that all the doors are locked. I make sure my weapon is ready, that it is with me, and that my wife's weapon is with her

Most farming communities now have a farm watch, through which farmers do their own patrols at night.
Fanus
By my gaan ek nie alleen uit nie. Baie mense kan se ek is bang, ek is nie bang nie, ek is net nie dom nie
Here at my place I don't go out alone. People can say I'm scared, I’m not scared, I’m just not stupid.

All of Fanus's direct neighbours have suffered attacks. When an attack happens, every other farmer is on the response team. This means that virtually every farmer has witnessed the horror perpetrated on a close friend
Fanus
Soos hier by my omgewing – oom Hennie my buurman, oom jan, wat ons langs-buurman is, by hannes kelly, by oom neels maritz. Dit was aanvalle, waar hulle gekap was, waar daar bloed was en waar daar dood was
Like here around me – uncle Hennie my neighbour, uncle Jan, our next neighbour, at James Kelly, at uncle Neels Maritz. These were attacks, where they were struck down, where there was blood and death.

Many view the senseless and extreme violence as a terror campaign aimed at driving the remaining farmers off their land.
Agrey
If you have observed a farm killing next to you or from a farmer that you know. Obviously you'll be totally discouraged, especially with your family, your wife and your kids

Agrey claims it only reaches the media when there are white people involved
Agrey
The people who feel that white farmers are really targeted, are the ones that are making an unneccessary noise about the whole issue. We don't see this as, when of course, any crime, we take it as just any other crime.

To many of these farmers their occupation is a calling, and central to that is our country's food security. Henry Geldenhuys from TAU-SA says we will all feel the loss of our farmers
Henry
Verseker speel plaasaanvalle en moorde 'n negatiewe rol ten opsigte van voedselsekerheid en kos op die tafel
Farm attacks and murders definitely have a negative impact on food security and on food on the table.

Ernst Roets from Afriforum agrees
Ernst
We're nearing the point where we're importing more food than we export, and we also find that land reform, farms taken from white people and given to black people, 90% of them have failed, according to government. So farmers are employers, and they are food creators and they have a very crucial role to play in this economy. When farmers aren't there anymore. The problems that we have, the debate about land reform would really be like an ant compared to an elephant if you compare this to hunger, to the mass amount of poverty and the problems this country would have if we did not have farmers.

But there is also another theory that instead of uplifting the poor, it is better to reach equality by breaking down all welfare not equally owned, including food security
BFLF
Black people aren't food secure. so when people talk about food security its based upon their own anxieties and fears that are unfairly intending their own wealth and not dealing with black people who are going hungry every single day

This week afriforum won a court interdict against Julius Malema
Ernst
We had julius malema and the leadership of the eff coming out, threatening that in april there was going to be this big uprising, they've actually started to encourage people to engage in illegal land grabs. So what weve done at afriforum with afri busness is approach the high court to get a court order. Prohibits malema as a person and the eff as an organistation to continue encouraging people to do this.
Julius
Afrikaner boys, die poppe sal dans. The EFF is coming for you boys. Afrikaner boys, the ANC expect you to think this place is still Orange Free State. This place is not Orange Free State. It is Free State. When we take over power, afrikaner mens, you will know your place
Ernest
One cannot just run away from anything if you are born into it, thats the way it has to happen
Fanie
Hierdie is my plaas, hierdie is my lewe, hierdie is my passie. Hoekom moet ek my passie opgee vir so iets
This is my farm, my life, my passion. Why should I give up my passion for something like this?
Fanus
Ek wil nie iets anders doen nie ek is hier, ek boer, dis my lewe. Dis my lewe en Levubu is my plek.
I don't want to do anything else – I’m here, I farm, this is my life. My life, and Levubu is my place.


10sec
February 2017 has seen the most farm murders over a 27 – year period. And March figures seem set to overtake this. What is really going on?

Brutal
15 sec
Is there a connection between farm attacks, brutal murders and the land redistribution debate?
Sound up: And so if black people are responding to that violence with violence – then they are well in their rights to take back land by any means neccesary.


15
Are farm murders random events, or carefully organised?
Sound up: Watse ek julle gaan gee daar is 'n balaclava, 'n gun en cash. Want hy se reguit hy is teen die boere
Who is behind these ongoing brutal murders?

The remoteness of the homesteads coupled with the relentless attacks, torture and murders changed their lifestyles forever. The farmers have been forced to take responsibility for their own safety Fanus Ek het staalhokke gemaak wat buite die vensters op is, dat hy nie kan inkom nie – 'n staalhok, met nog diefwering by die venster. Dot gaan my daai voorsprong gee. Ek gaan hoor as hy aan daai staalhok breek I made steel cages and put them up outside the windows, so that he cannot get in. A steel cage, still with burglar proofing on the windows also. It will give me that edge. I will hear when he tries to break the steel cage. Fanie is another levubu farmer who has had to adapt Fanie Hoe verkeerd is dit dat ek 'n kind van 10jaar en agt jaar moet leer om 'n wapen te hanteer. Net vir daai eendag ingeval, net as pappa of mamma seergekry het, en hulle moet hulleself kan verdedig How wrong is it that I have to teach a child of ten and one of 8 years old to handle a firearm? Just in case, for that one day, when daddy or mommy is injured and they have to defend themselves. And every day at sunset the idyllic surroundings make way for the same repetitive nightmare Herman Die aand het 'n ritueel waardeur jy gaan. Al jou wapens, jou kluis word oopgesluit, jou wapens word reggesit. Wapens word nagegaan, radios word getoets. Dis 'n heeltemaal ander lewe as wat ons gewoond was The evening has a ritual you have to go through. All your weapons… the gun safe is unlocked, you get the firearms in place. You check your guns, radios are tested. It is a totally different life to the one we were used to. Fanus Voor dit donker is, is ons in die huis, dan maak ek seker al die deure is gesluit. Ek maak seker my wapen is reg, is by my, my vrou se wapen is by haar. Before dark, we are in the house, then I check that all the doors are locked. I make sure my weapon is ready, that it is with me, and that my wife's weapon is with her Most farming communities now have a farm watch, through which farmers do their own patrols at night. Fanus By my gaan ek nie alleen uit nie. Baie mense kan se ek is bang, ek is nie bang nie, ek is net nie dom nie Here at my place I don't go out alone. People can say I'm scared, I’m not scared, I’m just not stupid. All of Fanus's direct neighbours have suffered attacks. When an attack happens, every other farmer is on the response team. This means that virtually every farmer has witnessed the horror perpetrated on a close friend Fanus Soos hier by my omgewing – oom Hennie my buurman, oom jan, wat ons langs-buurman is, by hannes kelly, by oom neels maritz. Dit was aanvalle, waar hulle gekap was, waar daar bloed was en waar daar dood was Like here around me – uncle Hennie my neighbour, uncle Jan, our next neighbour, at James Kelly, at uncle Neels Maritz. These were attacks, where they were struck down, where there was blood and death. Many view the senseless and extreme violence as a terror campaign aimed at driving the remaining farmers off their land. Agrey If you have observed a farm killing next to you or from a farmer that you know. Obviously you'll be totally discouraged, especially with your family, your wife and your kids Agrey claims it only reaches the media when there are white people involved Agrey The people who feel that white farmers are really targeted, are the ones that are making an unneccessary noise about the whole issue. We don't see this as, when of course, any crime, we take it as just any other crime. To many of these farmers their occupation is a calling, and central to that is our country's food security. Henry Geldenhuys from TAU-SA says we will all feel the loss of our farmers Henry Verseker speel plaasaanvalle en moorde 'n negatiewe rol ten opsigte van voedselsekerheid en kos op die tafel Farm attacks and murders definitely have a negative impact on food security and on food on the table. Ernst Roets from Afriforum agrees Ernst We're nearing the point where we're importing more food than we export, and we also find that land reform, farms taken from white people and given to black people, 90% of them have failed, according to government. So farmers are employers, and they are food creators and they have a very crucial role to play in this economy. When farmers aren't there anymore. The problems that we have, the debate about land reform would really be like an ant compared to an elephant if you compare this to hunger, to the mass amount of poverty and the problems this country would have if we did not have farmers. But there is also another theory that instead of uplifting the poor, it is better to reach equality by breaking down all welfare not equally owned, including food security BFLF Black people aren't food secure. so when people talk about food security its based upon their own anxieties and fears that are unfairly intending their own wealth and not dealing with black people who are going hungry every single day This week afriforum won a court interdict against Julius Malema Ernst We had julius malema and the leadership of the eff coming out, threatening that in april there was going to be this big uprising, they've actually started to encourage people to engage in illegal land grabs. So what weve done at afriforum with afri busness is approach the high court to get a court order. Prohibits malema as a person and the eff as an organistation to continue encouraging people to do this. Julius Afrikaner boys, die poppe sal dans. The EFF is coming for you boys. Afrikaner boys, the ANC expect you to think this place is still Orange Free State. This place is not Orange Free State. It is Free State. When we take over power, afrikaner mens, you will know your place Ernest One cannot just run away from anything if you are born into it, thats the way it has to happen Fanie Hierdie is my plaas, hierdie is my lewe, hierdie is my passie. Hoekom moet ek my passie opgee vir so iets This is my farm, my life, my passion. Why should I give up my passion for something like this? Fanus Ek wil nie iets anders doen nie ek is hier, ek boer, dis my lewe. Dis my lewe en Levubu is my plek. I don't want to do anything else – I’m here, I farm, this is my life. My life, and Levubu is my place. 10sec February 2017 has seen the most farm murders over a 27 – year period. And March figures seem set to overtake this. What is really going on? Brutal 15 sec Is there a connection between farm attacks, brutal murders and the land redistribution debate? Sound up: And so if black people are responding to that violence with violence – then they are well in their rights to take back land by any means neccesary. 15 Are farm murders random events, or carefully organised? Sound up: Watse ek julle gaan gee daar is 'n balaclava, 'n gun en cash. Want hy se reguit hy is teen die boere Who is behind these ongoing brutal murders?
